items.title: M3: A State-Event Generative Foundation Model for Market Microstructure Dynamics
items.desc: Proposes M3, a generative foundation model that jointly simulates order-flow events and limit-order-book liquidity rather than modelling them in isolation. Trained on large-scale order-level stock data, it shows predictable scaling behaviour and reproduces key market stylized facts for counterfactual microstructure simulation. [arXiv q-fin.CP/cs.LG, newly announced 2026-08-21]

items.title: CAT Bond Pricing with Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks
items.desc: Trains a Kolmogorov–Arnold Network on the residual from a closed-form lognormal baseline to price catastrophe bonds under a compound Poisson loss model, then extracts an interpretable symbolic pricing formula. The formula attains ~0.48% average relative pricing error on a disjoint holdout of 90,000 simulated prices. [arXiv q-fin.CP, newly announced 2026-08-21]

items.title: The Data Center Backlash Bursts Into the Midterms
items.desc: AI data-center buildout has become a central midterm campaign issue, with Democrats and a growing number of Republicans running ads tying data centers to rising household electricity bills. A review of TV and digital ads finds the theme spreading across Texas, Ohio, Michigan and Wisconsin races. [NYT, published 2026-08-23]

items.title: See the moment when Republican politicians turned against data centers
items.desc: A Washington Post text analysis of politicians' public statements finds Republican rhetoric on data centers turned sharply negative over the past six months, reversing earlier framing of them as pure economic upside for states like Ohio. Signals a shifting political economy around AI infrastructure siting and energy costs. [Washington Post, published 2026-08-23]

items.title: Harvard Is Selling a $699 Course Taught by A.I. Clones of Its Faculty
items.desc: Harvard Business School built interactive AI video avatars of its instructors for a paid entrepreneurship bootcamp, letting students pitch to an AI clone of a venture capitalist. DealBook tests the product and examines what monetizing faculty likenesses means for the economics of executive education. [NYT DealBook, published 2026-08-22]
